newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Army patrols Armenian capital, opposition lies low.
newsitem.headline: Army patrols Armenian capital, opposition lies low.

text.p: Thousands of troops backed by armoured vehicles patrolled the Armenian capital Yerevan for a second day on Friday following President Levon Ter-Petrosyan's presidential election victory.

Rival candidate Vazgen Manukyan, whose supporters took to the streets on Wednesday and clashed with riot police outside parliament, has accused Ter-Petrosyan of rigging the poll in which international observers noted several irregularities.

An interior ministry spokesman told Reuters that Manukyan had not been arrested, although six opposition members of parliament were detained on Thursday after the chamber voted to lift their immunity from prosecution.
"For now he (Manukyan) is free. He is in Yerevan. The organs who deal with these things probably know exactly where he is," said spokesman Vanush Shirmazanyan.
"Until the Central Electoral Commission gives us permission we cannot detain him," he added.
As a presidential candidate, Manukyan has special immunity from arrest until Sunday, Central Electoral Commission chief Khachik Bezirjyan said.

Manukyan, a former prime minister, says that he won Sunday's election. But unofficial results gave Ter-Petrosyan 52 percent of the votes compared with only 41 percent for Manukyan. Ter-Petrosyan just cleared the 50 percent barrier required to avoid a second-round runoff.

Shirmazanyan denied a report by Radio Liberty correspondent Genel Malbadyan that Manukyan was surrounded by about 10 armed security force members in a hallway of the parliament just before Thursday's session began.

The streets of Yerevan remained tense on Friday, with soldiers blocking off main streets and squares. Two independent radio stations which went off the air on Wednesday night were still not broadcasting.

An aide to Ter-Petrosyan said one soldier and one protester had been killed in the clashes outside parliament and dozens were hurt. Some protesters charged into the parliament building and beat the speaker and vice-speaker.
Ter-Petrosyan has since banned rallies and demonstrations, calling opposition politicians "mentally ill" people who had tried to stage a coup.

Ter-Petrosyan, 50, has led this small Caucasus country of 3.5 million since independence in 1991, a period marked by hardship caused largely by confrontation with neighbouring Azerbaijan over the disputed enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh.
Conditions have eased in recent months but Armenia has suffered many winters of power cuts and shortages.
